relevance_note: Multicentre paediatric cohort of '17 patients from 11 unrelated families' 'carrying a tumour necrosis factor alpha-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3) mutation', with per-patient genotypes in Table 3.
method_note: Read the full paper and transcribed every value by hand into a Python builder script (scratch directory); the script only assembled the JSON and checked that every span occurs verbatim and every row has every schema field. Table 3 values were re-checked against the table after the script ran. Labels: the paper numbers its cohort 'Patient 1'-'Patient 17' (Table 3 groups 'Patient 1–3' and 'Patient 10–13'; the text uses lower-case 'patient N'); each patient has its own row and the grouped Table 3 row is the label span. Relatives described only in the Genetic findings text are their own rows; the two nieces are labelled 'nieces of the grandfather (1 of 2)' / '(2 of 2)' (suffix added by me to keep two people apart). Variant rows for family-2 'Her mother'/'her grandfather' and the four family-8 relatives rest on the sentence 'Phenotypic heterogeneity, even among relatives carrying identical TNFAIP3 mutations' introducing those examples; no variant rows were made for the aunt, the two nieces or the cousin ('were reported to have'; testing not stated). POSSIBLE DUPLICATES: Table 3 puts Patients 10–13 in family 8, and the text describes patient 10's half-brother, half-sister, mother and maternal grandfather without saying which (if any) are Patients 11–13 (e.g. 'Their mother' has uveitis and the only cohort patient with ocular involvement is Patient 12; the half-brother has headache, as do Patients 11 and 13). They were NOT merged. Patient 14's complex allele is one variant row (text 'c. [29T>A; 49A>T], p. [(Leu10*); p. (Lys17*)]', table 'c. 29T>A; 49A>T | p. (Leu10*) p. (Lys17*)'). Variant class recorded only where the authors name it ('stop‐gain' for Arg87*, Arg183*, Trp164*; 'complex allele' for patient 14); fs/dup/splice/missense notation alone was not classed (the paper says 'only one missense variant was identified' without naming it). Zygosity is never stated per person (not reported). Sex is attributable only for Patient 4 ('Her mother') and Patient 10 ('His half-brother'); ethnicity, consanguinity (one consanguineous family, not identified), ages and colchicine use are cohort-level only. Group-statement exclusions (D-21) were applied to Patients 1–17 only, from statements naming every positive patient: ocular involvement (patient 12), autoimmune thyroiditis (1, 8), autoimmune diabetes (10), autoimmune hepatitis (6, 8), neurological symptoms (7, 11, 13), colitis (5, 7, 10, 12, 15, 17), pericarditis (4), and 'No patient' statements for connective tissue disease, isolated JIA and SLE. Checklist mappings: 'autoimmune diabetes' -> type 1 diabetes; headache counted as central nervous system involvement only for Patients 7, 11, 13, whom the paper groups as 'Neurological symptoms' (not for the half-brother); plain 'fever' was not counted as recurrent fever; unspecified 'ulcers'/'mucosal ulcers' were not mapped to oral or genital ulcers; gastritis and colonic ulcers count as gastrointestinal inflammation; Kawasaki disease was not mapped to vasculitis; 'asymptomatic' (patient 17's parent) was not turned into checklist exclusions. Patient 16 was previously reported (El Khouri et al^44); kept as a first-hand cohort row. CONTRADICTIONS/INCONSISTENCIES IN THE PAPER: abstract '17 patients from 11 unrelated families' vs results '11 unrelated, non-consanguineous families and one consanguineous family' and 12 families in Table 3; median age at diagnosis 13 years (text) vs 13.5 (Table 1); p.Pro457Alafs*16 called 'novel' yet 'present in Infevers database' and cited to ref 12; OTU variants '8/17 patients' vs 'Most of our patients (58 %)' vs Table 3 listing OTU for 15/17; hepatomegaly 2/17 clinically vs 3/15 on ultrasound; anakinra 'remission in 2/5 and partial improvement in 2/5' vs Table 4 effectiveness 2 (40); baricitinib 'partial clinical improvement' vs Table 4 effectiveness 0.
